rationale.complete: Round 1 done in two layers: replication on all 35 non-holdout periods (27 scorable for friction) plus four native tests (G51 roles, G12 judges, G16 operator rules, G38 loop-densest week), each with dated predictions. The correction sensor was validated blind (the a priori lexical marker failed and was replaced, Amendment 1). Synthetic validation on real structures found and fixed a targeting confound (Amendment 2). confirm.py is written and dry-run; it needs a small Jev pass that could not run (API credit). Not done: a high-recall sensor (so the immune test is underpowered), H16 TS3/TS4, any NE event study. Round 1c: stance v2.1 sensors (correct/decline classes, validated disagreement flag), label-noise null, synthetic re-validation with an amendment (A1c) before the real run, 51 estimates rows.
rationale.faithfulness: The friction model is refuted in reverse with adequate power: correctors receive warmer replies (meta rho -0.24, p 0.04), with no reply-level friction. The immune model is not testable at the sensor's recall (power 0.08-0.21 at a modest effect); point estimates are null or negative. Only descriptive HH210 coverage and the generic address effect hold. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H1 I0. 1c: friction reversal holds in the validated channel (rho -0.16, p 0.047); the blocked-spell immune test is now powered (0.96 at 1 logit) and null; loops remain underpowered.
rationale.usefulness: An operator learns two things: peer correction carries no social cost here (correctors are treated well), and the swarm almost never corrects a stuck agent (0.65% of loops; operator rules not peer-enforced), so error correction must be supplied from outside. The one lever (address a looping agent: +0.05 escape per message) is small, partly mechanical and echoes H29/H16.

one_line: Correctors draw less disagreement, not more (v2.1: ρ −0.16); read corrections do not end blocked spells (Δ +0.007, powered); being addressed raises loop escape by 5 points.

models.note: Viability value of corrections ~0 in blocked spells (powered, v2.1); loops underpowered

v2.claim: A read correction does not end blocked spells (Δ +0.007 [−0.053, +0.070], 337 treated windows, power 0.96), and agents who correct or decline more receive slightly less validated disagreement, the reverse of friction (ρ −0.16, p 0.047, 26 periods)

v2.decision: don't count on peer corrections to unstick blocked agents
v2.rater: coordinator, updated after round 1b (H55 round 1c); independent rater pending

v2_history.claim: Peer correction carries no stance cost: agents who correct more receive no colder, if anything warmer, replies (random-effects rho -0.24 [-0.44, -0.02] over 27 periods; replies to a correction no colder than to the same agent's other messages), and corrections almost never reach looping agents (0.65% of loop episodes vs 35% that receive any directed message).
